AT&T home Internet falls short, years after promising 100% coverage

Right now I'm getting a fraction of the promised speeds on Comcast's Extreme 105. Comcast sent a rep door to door offering very competitive bundle deals with a one year requirement. So now this area is over sold to hell. Comcast needs new routers and possibly a back bone upgrade.

A week later AT&T reps are going door to door, my block had just been upgraded to their 45Mbps U-verse. which is supposed to be the fiber to the home. Either way the park on my block allowed AT&T to run new fiber & install new hubs quickly and cheaply.

Which is why Comcast sent that rep out.

AT&T needs better advertising and to start making people offers. Actual Fiber to the home for a 1-2 year contract to cover the expense. I think that's reasonable.

In the rural areas AT&T should use their 4G LTE network/tech to provide connectivity the way Vivint does. Wireless internet to the home via a roof antenna and put a mesh network node tie in. To help boost the area and offer load balancing.
June 12th is when these companies will feel the sting of the people. Right now they are fighting tooth and nail to try and get free from net neutrality.

So I'm still relatively new to beard/moustache products so take my reviews with a grain of salt. I've only purchased 2 different beard oils and 2 moustache waxes.

Beard Oils:

Mr Natty's Famous Beard Elixir [R][E]

Does as you would expect, it softens the beard well and keeps the skin from feeling dry/irritated. The scent is pleasant and inoffensive. £8 for 10ml seemed a little steep when I purchased it. Also ran out rather quick but that was due to my overly generous application, I've since worked out how much to apply at a time.

Captain Fawcett's Ricki Hall's Booze & Baccy Beard Oil [R][C]

As far as beard feel it is great. Keeps it feeling soft, gives my black hair a nice shine and the scent is insane! It distracts my girlfriend as soon as she gets a hint of it. Reused my Mr Natty's dropper as a travel oil by transferring some of the Booze & Baccy into the empty dropper. Highly recommend.

Moustache Waxes:

Captain Fawcett's Ricki Hall's Booze & Baccy Moustache Wax [R][E]

Scent is again the biggest winning factor here and is why I still recommend it but it just doesn't have the hold I require. I find I need regular re-application to "Keep a stiff upper lip" as Captain Fawcett would say. It is still a nice moustache wax that I use regularly but for day to day stiffness I use another product. The price is £1 more but I believe that is due to this being a special product of the Captain's. Also comes in a tin which is a nice touch over the glass tub of the others in the Captain's lineup.

Captain Fawcett's Sandalwood Moustache Wax [R][C]

My daily, go to wax. Sandalwood is a pleasant scent and the hold is much stronger than the Booze & Baccy. Purchased back in October 2014 and am only just getting towards the bottom of the tub. Will be purchasing the expedition strength once the Sandalwood runs out.

Accessories:

Folding Pocket Moustache Comb with Leather Case [NR][E]

Bought this because my previous comb snapped when it fell out of my bag. It looks the part and the leather is genuine but the comb just doesn't feel right. The gold print lettering is already wearing off and I've only had it a couple weeks. As the comb and handle are in a straight line I have to practically drag my hand across my chin whilst combing my mo.

Overall I am still relatively inexperienced with these types of products but am so far happy with my purchases. I bought the Booze & Baccy gift set after sampling it at Beard at Somerset house. I've used samples in high street shops in London and haven't been overly impressed, generally preferring my current lineup.

Fintan awoke with a start, the coins dropping into his empty McDonalds cup sounded as if somebody had just rattled chains in his ears and for a moment he had thought he was back in jail. He looked down the street and saw the back of a woman on her way to work.

"Cheers, love. God knows I appreciate it." croaked Fintan before clearing his throat. It was unlikely she had heard him, but then again it was unlikely she would have responded to him in any case. He roused himself slowly.

"You're a free man Fintan, more free than all these suckers in the rat race." he chuckled to himself, wiping the sleep from his eyes with a dirty hand and peering around at the growing streams of early morning commuters with coffees and newspapers in hand. He ran a hand through his lank hair. It was beginning to mat together and every morning it was more difficult to pull his hand through without tearing his scalp off. He picked up his cup and took a look inside. Queen Elizabeth was looking back at him from the back of a coin.

"Alright Queenie, let's see how many twins you have this morning!" exclaimed Fintan. It was his favourite part of the day, emptying the coins onto the footpath beside him. "Come back to me Lizzie" he said as he caught one of the coins trying to roll away from him. He counted his per diem, a tidy £4.80. "Not bad for a nights work don't you think, Your Majesty?" said Fintan as he gathered the coins together and stowed them away inside his now baggy and worn corduroys, an acquisition from an earlier adventure involving strong cider, a dog and an unattended washing line.

He rose to his feet, leaving his scant collection of belongings behind him. Fintan felt no connection to these material items, all he felt was some unseen force compelling him down the street until at last he found himself in a corner store standing before a fridge. He opened the door and felt the cool air rushing around him. It was his favourite part of the day, reaching into the fridge and retrieving four cans of dry scrumpy.

"Alright me old buddies! How are yis today, good?" Fintan said to his new friends and promptly forgot about his old friends as he dropped them on the counter and strolled back into the bright London streets. He whistled a tune to himself, an old Irish song called "Dicey Reilly" that he always whistled when he was in such good company. He made his way back to where he had slept to find his belongings where he had left them. He settled himself down and placed three cans beneath his jacket to shield them from the sun. This was his favourite part of the day, cracking open the can. The bitter smell that emanated from it was as if somebody had mixed equal parts vinegar and piss together but to Fintan it was the most beautiful thing he had ever smelled. He raised the can to his bearded mouth and drank deeply, his stringy whiskers straining some of the residual pulp from the cheap cider.

"You're a good friend, to keep me refreshed like this" he said to his can, "I'd do it for you in a heartbeat, just say the word". He drank the rest of his can in one slurp, no mean feat considering scrumpy was only sold in 500ml cans. He discarded his dear friend just as fast as he got acquainted with another, opening it with glee. It was his favourite part of the day, feeling the alcohol starting to take effect. It was like a fire had been lit inside his stomach and the warmth of the flames danced up into his chest and face.

"Poor aul Dicey Reilly she has taken to the sup, poor aul Dicey Reilly she will never give it up" sang Fintan, no longer content with whistling as he was earlier, "It's off each morning to the pub, and then she's in for another little drop, ah the heart of the rule is Dicey Reilly". He had once been known for his singing voice, back in Ireland, but that seemed a lifetime ago and in many ways it was. A gentleman in a crisp shirt and trousers spilled some coins into the cup as he walked past without making eye contact.

"Dya think yer fuckin better than me is it, ya bollocks?" slurred Fintan as he tossed his now empty second can in the general direction of the long departed man and opened another. The alcohol was well and truly hitting him now as Fintan rose to unsteady feet and wobbled down a sidestreet to urinate. He returned to find the open can on it's side, it's precious cargo leaking onto the concrete like a British oil rig spilling oil into the Gulf of Mexico. He ran to save what little he could but there was only a dribble left, which he drank down before throwing the can down onto the ground in anger.

He sat himself back down and opened his final can before starting to sing again. Fintan was sure that he was singing beautifully, he always did after all, but all the passersby were either avoiding him like they would the plague or trying not to laugh as they made their way down the street. Fintan was oblivious as he was getting so into his singing that he had closed his eyes.

"Oi! Shut up you drunken Irish bastard!" shouted somebody from a shop across the street, "Every fucking day I have to listen to this shit, I've had enough of it. I'm calling the coppers.". Fintan shouted something unintelligable back at the shop worker before returning to his last can, which he finished with a couple of hefty swigs. He looked about him and the city seemed to be spinning slightly, causing Fintan to feel slightly nauseous. As inebriated as he was, he knew it would be a waste to vomit the alcohol now after he had just finished it so he decided to lie down for a nap. It was his favourite time of the day, having a midday siesta in the middle of London while the rest of the fools rushed about chasing money.

Fintan awoke again to the sound of coins with a smile. He opened his eyes to find a large man in a uniform jangling leg-irons in his ear.

"Get up prisoner."
